topic_names: AC Voltage Applied to a Capacitor
why: The answer depends on the current in a pure capacitor leading the voltage by exactly 90 degrees, which makes the power factor cos(90) = 0, so the energy drawn in each quarter cycle is returned in the next and the net energy consumed over a full cycle is zero.
note: The same 90-degree lead also rules out options 2, 3 and 4, so this one topic carries every discriminating fact; 'Power in an AC Circuit' is the near neighbour for the zero-average-power half of the argument.
